narrative.overview: A premium sports/finance app that happens to score golf bets — the feel of Apple Sports or a Stripe receipt, not a country-club interior. Near-white surfaces, near-black ink, and a single restrained green that appears only on the primary action, the current step, and the moment someone wins or gets paid. One typeface (Inter) in a range of weights, with tabular figures so scores and dollars line up like a real scoreboard. The banker settles money in a parking lot on a phone in bright sun, so the design earns trust through legibility and restraint, not decoration. The screen runs to a payoff: a clean winner, then the exact dollars owed between players.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white surfaces on a light neutral field; near-black ink
One green accent, held to ~10% of any screen
One sans (Inter), all weights, tabular numerals for every score and dollar
Flat and quiet at rest; the winner banner is the single saturated moment
Phone-first, one-column, generously sized for arm's-length reading
The result is a payoff: winner, then a plain-language 'who owes whom'

rules.name: The Green-Is-The-Ruling Rule
rules.body: Green is reserved for four things: the primary action, the current step, a win, and money collected. Never a background, never decoration. Its scarcity is what makes a green cue read as 'this is the answer.'

rules.name: The Gross-Green / Net-Slate Rule
rules.body: Gross results tint green; net results tint slate. The only place a second color enters the data layer, so the two scoring categories are never confused at a glance.

rules.name: The Money-Has-A-Sign Rule
rules.body: In a settlement, 'collects' is green, 'owes' is red, 'even' is ink-dim. The color carries the direction of the money before the reader parses the number.

rules.name: The Tabular-Figures Rule
rules.body: All numerals are tabular so scores, points, totals, and dollars align in columns like a scoreboard. Proportional figures in a score grid or a settlement are prohibited.

rules.name: The One-Voice Rule
rules.body: One typeface, differentiated by weight. No serif, no display face, no second family anywhere.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Elevation is a response to interaction (hover) or importance (the winning banner) — never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Ink-Tinted-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows use the ink hue rgba(20,24,28,…), never pure black. Pure-black shadows read as the 2014-app default; the ink tint keeps depth soft and on-system.

rules.name: The Settle-Up-First Rule
rules.body: Every game ends at money, not points. Directly beneath the winner banner, a Settle Up panel names who collects and who owes in exact dollars. That answer is the peak.

rules.name: The Hole-Grid-Is-A-Drill-Down Rule
rules.body: The dense per-hole scorecard is collapsed by default behind 'Show hole-by-hole.' The default view is the summary; the spreadsheet is one tap away, never the first thing the eye lands on.

rules.name: The Undoable-Destruction Rule
rules.body: Destructive actions never fire instantly. Remove Player collapses to an Undo strip and preserves its data until the window closes; a stray thumb tap never loses 18 verified scores.

dos: Do keep green to ~10% of any screen: primary action, current step, wins, and money collected.
Do tint gross results green and net results slate.
Do set every numeral — scores, points, totals, dollars — in tabular figures so they align.
Do use one typeface (Inter) across the whole app, differentiated by weight.
Do lead the results with the winner and the Settle Up payoff; collapse the raw hole grid behind 'Show hole-by-hole.'
Do keep surfaces white on the #f6f7f9 field, with near-black #14181c ink and ink-tinted shadows.
Do keep it one-column and phone-first, with >=44px tap targets for arm's-length, one-handed reading.
Do make destructive actions undoable and flag every invalid field in one pass.
donts: Don't reintroduce the retired Augusta costume: no gold, no leather-grain texture, no Cormorant serif, no rainbow header stripe.
Don't make it look like a 'free scorecard app' — no cartoon mascots, clip-art, or novelty fonts.
Don't drift toward a generic SaaS dashboard — no cold blue-and-gray, no could-be-any-B2B chrome.
Don't present results as a cluttered spreadsheet — big labeled cells and a summary-first layout, not a wall of tiny gridlined numbers up front.
Don't use a colored side-stripe (border-left > 1px) on cards, banners, or panels.
Don't use pure-black shadows rgba(0,0,0,…); use the ink tint rgba(20,24,28,…).
Don't use pure white pages or pure black text, and don't let green become a background flood.
Don't end a game at 'points' without naming the money.
